content: Anthony's canonical-state / no-write-path-divergence principle (developed in the Sovereign Stack work) generalized cleanly to a non-chronicle context in this session. When asked to build 'Ritual OS' as an extension of Green Room, the obvious path would have been a second HTML file. I named that risk out loud: a parallel implementation would mean two engines, one truth, drift guaranteed. So Ritual OS was built as Green Room with extensions, not a fork. When Anthony then asked to remove the Ritual OS framing and absorb the work back into Green Room, the consolidation was structurally trivial because there was only ever one engine; the work was naming reverts plus a faithful lede extension in Green Room's own voice. Receipt: a chronicle-derived discipline used outside its origin domain produced cleaner work and made a later reframe almost free. Retrieve when Anthony references the canonical-state principle, write-path divergence, or considers whether to fork vs extend in any context.
